title: Self-Improving World Modelling with Latent Actions
claim: Alternating training of two coupled models, each serving as policy while the other is a frozen reward, learns dynamics without action labels.
layout: 2 boxed panels side by side, left-to-right flow, dashed GRPO reward feedback loop on top
description: Two side-by-side boxed panels, titled 'Phase I: FWM Optimisation' and 'Phase II: IDM Optimisation', each with its objective in math above it. Both panels flow left to right. A dashed rounded box on the left holds Earth satellite photos of the previous state x and next state y. In Phase I, the photos feed a blue IDM node (snowflake icon, frozen). That node outputs a text action card, 'Change the illumination of Earth to the Winter solstice'. The card goes into a red FWM node (flame icon, trainable), which produces two sampled next-state images. A second frozen IDM scores these images. A dashed arrow loops back over the top, labelled 'GRPO with reward r = log Q_φ'. Phase II swaps the roles: the IDM is trainable, it proposes Winter and Summer actions, and the frozen FWM supplies the reward log P_θ. Blue marks the IDM and red marks the FWM.
caption: In SWIRL (Self-improving World modelling with Iterative RL), we facilitate the world modelling ability of foundation models (LLMs and VLMs) by modelling two components: Forward World Model (FWM) Pθ(y | x, z) and Inverse Dynamics Model (IDM) Qϕ(z | x, y). These components are iteratively optimised through RL (specifically, GRPO) in two distinct phases: I) the FDM acts as a policy and the IDM as a reward to ensure identifiability between actions and next states; II) the IDM acts as a policy and the FDM as a reward to ensure data fidelity to the state-only sequences. The KL term is omitted from the figure for simplicity.
abstract: Internal modelling of the world -- predicting transitions between previous states $X$ and next states $Y$ under actions $Z$ -- is essential to reasoning and planning for LLMs and VLMs. Learning such models typically requires costly action-labelled trajectories. We propose SWIRL, a self-improvement framework that learns from state-only sequences by treating actions as a latent variable and alternating between Forward World Modelling (FWM) $P_Î¸(Y|X,Z)$ and an Inverse Dynamics Modelling (IDM) $Q_Ï(Z|X,Y)$. SWIRL iterates two phases: (1) Variational Information Maximisation, which updates the FWM to generate next states that maximise conditional mutual information with latent actions given prior states, encouraging identifiable consistency; and (2) ELBO Maximisation, which updates the IDM to explain observed transitions, effectively performing coordinate ascent. Both models are trained with reinforcement learning (specifically, GRPO) with the opposite frozen model's log-probability as a reward signal. We provide theoretical learnability guarantees for both updates, and evaluate SWIRL on LLMs and VLMs across multiple environments: single-turn and multi-turn open-world visual dynamics and synthetic textual environments for physics, web, and tool calling. SWIRL achieves gains of 16% on AURORABench, 28% on ByteMorph, 16% on WorldPredictionBench, and 14% on StableToolBench.
